prerequisites.instruction: Confirm the selected Google account, Workspace Developer Preview membership and enrolled Google Cloud project. Preview features are not for public applications before general availability; access outside the domain/company requires any explicit permission offered and granted by Google. This catalog does not establish eligibility or permission.

Enable calendar-json.googleapis.com and calendarmcp.googleapis.com in the selected project. Configure consent, audience/test users and a host-appropriate OAuth client with the actual redirect URI, not a copied example redirect.

The guide sample scopes are https://www.googleapis.com/auth/calendar.calendarlist.readonly, https://www.googleapis.com/auth/calendar.events.freebusy and https://www.googleapis.com/auth/calendar.events.readonly. They do not grant mutation authority despite the advertised create/update/delete/respond tools. The existing credential and policy owners verify selected account/calendar and scopes for each requested operation, with separate consent if required. No automatic scope expansion or credential fallback is supplied.
Confirm project service-enablement permissions and any Workspace administrator restrictions on the selected OAuth app, account and scopes.

Meet Google's prompt/response screening requirement using Model Armor or the host's documented alternative accepted by users. The host chooses and authorizes processors, permissions, routing and logging; Model Armor logging can include full payloads. Do not implicitly enable an external processor or transmit content to one.

Bind the exact connection, current tool schemas, bounded operations, credential owner, policy and lifecycle in the existing ActivationManifest. Account, calendar, scope and role readiness need owner-authenticated receipts; offline selection validation is only a declaration.

Select and verify the retained Python source checkpoint described in SUPPORT.md or a separately verified artifact containing it. Use Python 3.11+ and the google-calendar extra with HTTPX >=0.28.1,<0.29 and AnyIO >=4.13,<5. No public PyPI release or TypeScript Calendar implementation is claimed.

Enable calendar-json.googleapis.com in the selected project and configure consent/audience, any required verification and an OAuth client appropriate for the actual host. Reuse the existing credential owner; this recipe is not an OAuth implementation.
Explicitly select the account and calendar resource. A calendar ID, including primary, is not proof that the selected credential belongs to that account or may access that calendar.

The host supplies the authenticated HTTPX client and optional per-request auth binding for the selected account, API base and calendar. Choose the least required scopes for the selected reads or mutations; read-only scopes cannot authorize writes. Existing owners retain secrets, refresh/revoke and account correspondence. No ambient credential lookup or retry after authentication failure is supplied.
Resolve applicable organization app/access restrictions for the requested account, calendar and scopes before use.

Compose the five operations into the existing service export and retain host authorization, bounded paging, cancellation and cleanup. In a host that has them, retain internal-calendar raw-write denial, origin stamping, the existing write-version ledger, semantic publisher, deterministic IDs, conditional ETags and final readback. An unknown write outcome requires owner reconciliation, never automatic resend, replacement ID or switching strategy. No crash-safe fencing or exactly-once delivery is supplied.

blockers: The host must bind the selected Python SDK source or separately verified artifact, selected account/calendar, operation schemas and lifecycle to the existing service export. The operation library is not an activated tool surface.

The existing host credential owner must supply OAuth registration, account consent, minimal operation scopes and credential refresh/revoke. This recipe adds no credential storage, OAuth flow or authentication fallback.
The retained source checkpoint and local protocol tests do not establish public package availability, live Google access, current account authorization or complete host adoption.
